question:
The in-house development team at an accounting firm reviews pull requests for a tax calculation library using a Claude Code CI review. Currently, an average of 14 findings per PR are all posted as inline comments. However, developers have actually acted on only about 30% of the findings, and the comments are increasingly going unread.

The team wants to change its process so that only important findings are commented on immediately, and the rest are reviewed in a weekly batch. For the past three months of findings, there is a record of whether developers chose to address or dismiss each one.

Which design for triaging findings is most appropriate?

choices.A: In the same session that generated the findings, have Claude assign a confidence score from 1 to 10, and post findings scoring 7 or higher as immediate comments as-is.
choices.B: Regardless of severity, limit immediate comments to the top 3 per PR and defer the rest to the weekly review.
choices.C: Have a separate verification pass assign a confidence score to each finding, and triage using a threshold calibrated against the past records of how developers responded.
choices.D: Add “Report only high-confidence findings” to the review prompt and post all output as immediate comments.

question:
A pharmaceutical company operates a customer support resolution agent that handles product inquiries from medical institutions. Currently, the application is designed to automatically transfer the case to a human agent when either of the following applies.

The sentiment analysis score falls below a certain level

The agent's self-reported confidence falls below 0.6

Analysis of one month of logs showed that 43% of transferred cases could have been resolved with standard procedures, such as complaints about shipping delays. Meanwhile, inquiries about off-label use and adverse event reports, submitted in a calm tone, were answered by the agent itself with confidence remaining around 0.9.

Internal regulations require that these two types always be handled by a representative of the medical information department.

Which is the most likely root cause?

choices.A: The sentiment analysis threshold is too strict, so cases from customers with a calm tone are not being routed to human agents.
choices.B: The escalation conditions are implemented only in application code, not in the agent's system prompt.
choices.C: The confidence threshold of 0.6 is too low, so answers with confidence around 0.9 fall outside the escalation criteria.
choices.D: The escalation decision relies on tone and self-reported confidence, which are not tied to the content of the case.

question:
The policy planning division of a prefectural government is using a multi-agent research system to investigate the effectiveness of child-rearing support measures by municipality. The coordinator passes the following steps to the search subagent in its prompt.

Search the national statistics site

Summarize the top 3 results

Return the results

Reviewing the results, for topics where the national statistics site has no municipality-level data, the search subagent simply returned “該当なし” and finished. In fact, in many cases the needed data existed in public materials from prefectures and cities. There were also cases where it summarized and returned old statistics from 2019 or earlier.

Which are appropriate changes to how the coordinator delegates to the search subagent? (Select two.)

choices.A: Communicate the purpose of the research and the quality criteria: municipality-level, 2020 or later, and primary sources.
choices.B: Enable the setting that lets the subagent inherit the coordinator's entire conversation history, and convey the background.
choices.C: Specify the types and scope of permitted information sources as conditions, and leave the search order to the subagent.
choices.D: Add a procedure: if nothing is found on the national statistics site, search the prefectural site, then the city site.

question:
The research division of a public research institute uses a multi-agent research system to produce research reports on policy themes. In 12 of the past 30 reports, reviewers pointed out that “major areas of the theme are missing.”

For example, for the theme “The impact of population aging on regional public transportation,” the coordinator's log recorded the following three subtasks, one per type of information source.

Investigate white papers and statistics

Investigate academic papers

Investigate news articles

All three subagents searched the wording of the theme as is, and most of the returned results concerned the abolition of local bus routes. Areas of the theme such as railways, demand-responsive transport, and the mobility needs of older adults did not appear in any of the instructions.

Which change would be most effective in preventing gaps in the report?

choices.A: Increase the number of search results each subagent retrieves from 10 to 30.
choices.B: Have the coordinator identify the areas that make up the theme and assign a separate research scope to each area.
choices.C: Add a subtask that investigates municipal public materials, increasing the types of information sources to four.
choices.D: Add a list of search keywords to each information-source subtask.

question:
The development team at a logistics company uses Claude Code to generate code for a delivery route calculation service. The team has the following conventions.

Handle distances as integers in meters

Set a timeout on external API calls

These conventions are followed in the lead developer's session. However, they are not followed in the sessions of the three members who joined this month, or in Claude Code run in CI.

When /context is run in the lead developer's session, CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md appear under Memory files. In a new member's session, only CLAUDE.md appears, and its content was only build and test commands.

Which is the most likely cause?

choices.A: The root CLAUDE.md is too long, so loading is cut off partway in new environments.
choices.B: The new members launched Claude Code in a subdirectory, so the root CLAUDE.md is not loaded.
choices.C: The new members' ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is empty, so the project settings are not inherited.
choices.D: The conventions are written in the lead developer's CLAUDE.local.md and are not shared through Git.

question:
The development team at a travel company audits fare rule determination logic with Claude Code. One developer has been analyzing 25 files related to fare rules in a session named fare-audit.

The next day, a pull request merged by a colleague changed three of these files: fare_rules.py, discount.py, and tax_calc.py. The other 22 files are unchanged. The developer wants to continue the audit, making the most of the previous day's analysis.

Which method of resuming work is most appropriate?

choices.A: Start a new session and have Claude load and analyze all 25 files again from scratch.
choices.B: Resume with claude --resume fare-audit and have Claude re-analyze only the three changed files.
choices.C: Resume with claude --resume fare-audit and have Claude continue the previous work without mentioning the changes.
choices.D: Resume with claude --continue and instruct only “Check the latest state and then continue.”

question:
A city hall operates a customer support resolution agent that handles residents' bulky waste collection reservations and mailed applications for various certificates. The MCP tools that make reservations and applications return a uniform error message, “処理に失敗しました”, for every kind of failure.

The logs revealed the following.

For a reservation that violated the rule “collection requests must be made by 5 p.m. three days before the collection date,” the agent repeated the same reservation four times and failed each time

For an application specifying a nonexistent address code, the resident was told “システム障害が発生しています”

Which are appropriate improvements to the tool's error response? (Select two.)

choices.A: Keep the uniform error message and have the agent escalate to a human agent whenever a tool fails.
choices.B: Keep the uniform error message and have the agent retry any failure up to three times at intervals.
choices.C: Return the type of failure and whether it can be resolved by retrying as structured metadata.
choices.D: For failures caused by rule violations, return a clear explanation that can be relayed to the resident as is.

question:
The development team at a SaaS company uses Claude Code for code generation in a monorepo. They compiled GraphQL schema and resolver conventions in .claude/rules/graphql.md and specified paths: ["**/*.{graphql,ts}"] in the frontmatter.

The conventions should apply only to the following files.

All .graphql files in the repository

Files whose names end in .resolver.ts

The target files are deep in each package's hierarchy, such as packages/billing/src/graphql/ and packages/admin/src/resolvers/.

However, these conventions were being loaded every time even when editing ordinary TypeScript files unrelated to GraphQL.

Which are correct paths specifications? (Select two.)

choices.A: Specify paths: ["**/*.graphql", "**/*.ts"].
choices.B: Specify paths: "**/*.graphql,**/*.resolver.ts".
choices.C: Specify paths: ["packages/*/*.graphql", "packages/*/*.resolver.ts"].
choices.D: Specify paths: ["**/*.graphql", "**/*.resolver.ts"].

question:
The development team at a publishing company is using Claude Code to modify their article distribution system (CMS). One developer has spent over three hours in a single session investigating the processing flow from article publication to cache invalidation. Early in the session, they told Claude, “The cache layer code is owned by another team, so do not change it.”

Later in the session, however, the following changes appeared in Claude's behavior.

It began searching again with Grep for files it had finished investigating earlier, such as ArticleRepository.ts

It even started proposing fixes that rewrite CacheInvalidator

Checking with /context showed that conversation history occupied most of the context, much of it long Grep and Read output. CLAUDE.md has not been changed during this time.

Which is the most likely cause?

choices.A: The context is filled with a large amount of tool output, making it hard to refer to earlier investigation results and instructions.
choices.B: The files under investigation were changed by another member partway through, and Claude is re-reading them.
choices.C: Automatic compaction lost CLAUDE.md, so Claude can no longer refer to the project conventions.
choices.D: An outdated entry in CLAUDE.md encouraging changes to the cache layer remains, and it is being prioritized in the later part of the session.

question:
The admissions office of a university is about to introduce a structured data extraction system that extracts course names, credits, grades, and expected graduation dates from transcripts submitted by transfer applicants. Overall accuracy measured on 2,000 validation items was 97%, above the target of 95%. The team is considering ending human review for extractions with a confidence of 0.9 or higher.

The submitted transcripts come in various types, including PDFs from domestic universities, English-language documents from overseas universities, and scanned images with handwritten annotations.

Which are appropriate things to do before reducing human review? (Select two.)

choices.A: Since overall accuracy exceeded the target, uniformly end review for all extractions with confidence 0.9 or higher.
choices.B: Measure accuracy separately by document type (domestic, overseas, with handwritten annotations) and by field.
choices.C: Randomly select 50 items from the validation data and recheck them; if accuracy is 95% or higher, end review across the board.
choices.D: Reduce human review only for segments that meet the 95% target, and continue review for the other segments.

question:
The development team at a consumer goods manufacturer runs a CI job that reviews pull requests with Claude Code and outputs the findings as JSON. The output is checked by a validation script, and is considered a failure in the following cases.

It cannot be parsed as JSON

A finding's line number is outside the range of the PR's diff

On failure, the job instructs “The previous output was invalid. Try again.” and re-runs up to 5 times.

Over the past month, 23% of runs failed validation; of these, 60% were JSON syntax errors and 40% were line numbers outside the diff range. Cases that fail even after 5 retries continue to occur.

Which are appropriate improvements to the validation and retry mechanism? (Select two.)

choices.A: On each retry, start a new run and tell Claude only “The previous attempt failed,” passing the same diff.
choices.B: Include the failed output and the original diff in the retry, and specify concretely which value in which finding is invalid and why.
choices.C: Raise the retry limit from 5 to 10 and run with the same instruction until it succeeds.
choices.D: Fix the output schema with --json-schema to eliminate JSON syntax errors.

question:
A shipping company is building a customer support resolution agent that handles container transport inquiries. The MCP tool lookup_booking throws an exception when the booking number format is incorrect or the booking has been cancelled, and the MCP server returns it as a JSON-RPC error response.

Checking the logs, in 72% of such cases the agent ended the conversation by answering “システム障害のため確認できません”. Almost none of the cases involved asking the customer for the booking number again or telling the customer that the booking had been cancelled.

Which way of returning lookup_booking failures is most appropriate?

choices.A: Retry three times within the server before throwing an exception, and return an error only if it still fails.
choices.B: Return the failure as a tool result with isError: true, and write the reason for the failure and possible next actions in content.
choices.C: Keep isError as false even on failure, and return content that says “エラー: 予約番号が無効です”.
choices.D: Return it as a JSON-RPC error response as is, with a detailed reason for the failure in message.

question:
The development team at a property and casualty insurance company develops an insurance claims system with Claude Code. Person A created a custom slash command /claim-validate that compiles the claim data validation procedure, intending for everyone on the team to use it.

The command works in A's environment, but even after the other five members update their repository to the latest state, /claim-validate does not appear in the command list. The repository's .claude/ directory contains only settings.json, with no commands/ or skills/.

Which is the most likely cause and remedy?

choices.A: The command is in a personal location, so move it to .claude/commands/ and commit it.
choices.B: The other members' Claude Code versions are outdated, so everyone should update.
choices.C: The command file has no frontmatter, so add description and reload.
choices.D: The command name duplicates an existing skill, so recreate it with a different name.

question:
An agricultural supplies mail-order company operates a customer support resolution agent that handles inquiries about orders for fertilizer and farm machinery parts. About 21% of inquiries contain multiple requests, such as “The fertilizer from last week still hasn't arrived. I think I was also charged twice. Also, I'd like to know whether the tractor part I ordered fits my model.”

The logs show that in such inquiries, the agent often resolves only the first request and ends the conversation, leading to a stream of repeat inquiries from customers. The first-contact resolution rate is 61%, well below the target of 80%.

Which improvement is most effective?

choices.A: Process requests one at a time in order, starting a new conversation for each request and redoing identity verification from get_customer.
choices.B: Decompose the inquiry into separate requests, share the verified customer information, investigate each request in parallel, and combine the results into a single response.
choices.C: For inquiries containing multiple requests, ask the customer to resubmit each request as a separate inquiry.
choices.D: When an inquiry containing multiple requests is detected, escalate to a human agent without checking the content.

question:
The engineering research team at an automotive parts manufacturer builds a multi-agent research system with the Claude Agent SDK. The coordinator delegates work to four subagents: web search, document analysis, synthesis, and report generation. The coordinator's prompt says “Call all four subagents in order for every question.”

Usage analysis showed the following.

About 60% of questions are single fact checks such as “the effective date of a certain standard,” but even these go through all four subagents, so each takes an average of 4 minutes and costs $0.90 per question

The document analysis subagent is launched every time, even for questions with no attached documents, and returns “分析対象なし”

Which are appropriate changes to the coordinator's design? (Select two.)

choices.A: Stop calling the four subagents in order and instead launch all four in parallel every time.
choices.B: Place a classification model trained on past questions in front of the coordinator and have it predict which subagents to call.
choices.C: State in each subagent's description the work it handles and what kinds of questions it should be called for.
choices.D: Drop the fixed call-order instruction and have the coordinator analyze the question's requirements and call only the necessary subagents.

question:
The student support office of a university operates a structured data extraction system that extracts application category, household income, and enrollment status from scholarship application documents. In the extraction tool's JSON schema, the application category is defined as an enum with three values: “給付型”, “貸与型”, and “授業料減免”.

Beginning this fiscal year, applications in new categories, such as study abroad support and special disaster provisions, have started to arrive. Auditing the extraction results showed that many of these applications were classified as “授業料減免”, and about 9% of all applications were registered in the downstream screening system with the wrong category.

New categories are expected to increase by several types each year.

Which are appropriate changes to schema design and operation? (Select two.)

choices.A: Add “other” to the enum and provide a detail string field to record the content.
choices.B: Periodically tally applications for which no category fit, and add frequently occurring ones to the enum as official values.
choices.C: Drop the application category enum, make it a free-text string, and have Claude return the category name exactly as written in the document.
choices.D: Add “Always choose the closest of the three categories” to the prompt to reduce classification variability.

question:
A game company builds a developer productivity tool with the Claude Agent SDK and uses it to investigate crash reports. The agent retrieves data from three MCP servers, whose response formats are as follows.

The crash collection service returns timestamps in Unix milliseconds

The build server returns timestamps in ISO 8601 with +09:00

The matchmaking server returns status as numeric codes such as 3 and 7

All three are external services and the response formats cannot be changed.

According to the logs, in 11% of investigations the agent misjudged the order of events, such as concluding “ビルドの配布後にクラッシュが増えた”. The system prompt contains text explaining the time formats, but errors have not decreased.

Which countermeasure is most reliable?

choices.A: Concatenate the responses of the three servers as is into one tool result and leave chronological judgment to Claude.
choices.B: Use a PostToolUse hook to normalize the time and status formats before Claude receives them.
choices.C: Put each server's time format and a status code mapping table in the system prompt, and have Claude convert before judging.
choices.D: Use a PreToolUse hook to add an output format specification to each tool's input and have the servers return ISO 8601.

question:
The development team at a precision instruments manufacturer has Claude Code generate tests for the previous day's changes in a nightly CI job. The job script runs with claude -p, and when it finishes, it uses a regular expression to pick out the part of the standard output text that says “N件のテストを生成しました”, and tallies the number of generated tests and target files.

Over the past month, two problems occurred.

On a day when the authentication configuration expired and no tests were generated, the script treated the run as successful and proceeded to subsequent jobs

Whenever Claude's phrasing changed, such as to “テストを3件追加しました”, the regular expression failed to match and the tally broke

Which are appropriate responses for this CI job? (Select two.)

choices.A: Instruct in the prompt to “write at the end in the format ‘生成件数: N’”, and have the regular expression pick up that line.
choices.B: Check claude's exit code and treat the job as failed if it is nonzero.
choices.C: Receive the result in structured form with --output-format json and --json-schema.
choices.D: Raise the --max-turns value so that test generation continues to the end without being cut off midway.

question:
A staffing agency operates a structured data extraction system. The system extracts work history, skills, and desired conditions from resumes (PDFs) sent by applicants, validates them against a JSON schema, and registers them in the candidate database. Extraction is handled by a subagent, which is currently configured to use all 18 tools in the whole system.

Checking the logs revealed the following.

The extraction subagent makes 40 calls per week that write unvalidated data directly to the candidate database

Calls that web-search information about the employer the applicant applied to occur an average of 3 times per case

About 60% of extractions require looking up the job code master, and currently each time processing is handed back to the coordinator

Which are appropriate changes to the extraction subagent's tool configuration? (Select two.)

choices.A: Narrow the extraction subagent's tools to only those needed for reading documents and submitting extraction results.
choices.B: Give the extraction subagent read and write permissions to the entire candidate database, including the job code master.
choices.C: Add a read-only lookup_job_code tool that can query only the job code master.
choices.D: Leave the tool configuration unchanged and instruct in the system prompt, “Do not write to the candidate database or perform web searches.”

question:
The e-commerce development team at a retail chain automatically reviews pull requests with Claude Code and comments on each finding with a severity of critical, major, or minor. The severity definitions are written in the review system prompt only as “judge according to the magnitude of impact.”

A recent audit found the following inconsistencies in determinations.

A missing null check in a function that calculates payment amounts was judged critical in one PR and minor in another

A variable naming inconsistency was in one case judged major

Among developers, a tendency has spread to skim comments without looking at severity.

Which measure is most effective for making severity determination consistent?

choices.A: Add “Judge severity carefully, and if unsure, choose the lower one” to the system prompt.
choices.B: Have each finding output a confidence score along with severity, and post only findings with confidence of 0.8 or higher.
choices.C: Add the criteria for each severity level, together with concrete code examples, to the system prompt.
choices.D: Reduce severity to two levels, “important” and “other,” to reduce room for uncertainty in determination.

question:
The development team at a restaurant reservation service is about to use Claude Code to implement a feature that registers a waitlist for fully booked time slots and notifies people in order when openings appear. The developer in charge has never built a waitlist mechanism and plans to ask, “Build a waitlist feature.”

In the past, a feature built from a similar request failed to account for the following and had to be rebuilt after release.

The order of notification when two cancellations occur at the same time

How to handle a failed notification

Which are appropriate ways to proceed with implementing this feature? (Select two.)

choices.A: Write the behavior for simultaneous cancellations and notification failures into the spec as acceptance criteria, and then begin implementation.
choices.B: Before implementation, have Claude ask questions about design considerations to surface issues that had not been anticipated.
choices.C: Without having Claude ask the developer questions, have it write a detailed design document alone and then begin implementation.
choices.D: Have Claude assume a generally reasonable spec and implement immediately, fixing problems in review.

question:
A live entertainment company operates a customer support resolution agent that handles ticket refund and seat change requests. The agent extracts quantity, performance date, and purchase date from the customer's message and passes them to the refund request tool.

Investigation of the logs showed that for inquiries with casual expressions such as “I think it was 2 or 3 tickets” and “I bought them around the end of last month,” the agent filled in the quantity as 3 and the purchase date as an end-of-month date by guesswork and submitted the request. Cases that later required correction numbered 140 per month.

The system prompt describes the extraction procedure in detail in prose, but contains no examples.

Which are appropriate ways to use few-shot examples to reduce extraction hallucinations? (Select two.)

choices.A: Add an example response in which, for expressions where the value cannot be pinned down to one, the field is left empty and the customer is asked to confirm.
choices.B: Add few-shot examples to the prompt that show casual expressions such as “2 or 3 tickets” together with the correct extraction result.
choices.C: Show example outputs of an extraction tool that makes quantity and purchase date required fields, and have it always fill in values when submitting.
choices.D: Do not add examples; instead add emphasis in the system prompt: “Never fill in values by guessing.”

question:
The IT department of an international cooperation NGO builds a developer productivity tool with the Claude Agent SDK and uses it to investigate legacy code of a donation management system. One developer has been investigating for over two hours in a single session the processing flow from donation intake to receipt issuance.

In the first half of the session, the agent had identified the specific dependencies between ReceiptIssuer and DonationLedger. In the second half, however, the agent began answering based on typical patterns rather than the class names identified earlier, such as “一般的には、台帳クラスが領収書を発行します”. Most of the context is occupied by long Grep and Read output.

The developer wants to continue the same investigation while carrying over the findings so far.

Which is the most appropriate response?

choices.A: Start a new session and, without conveying the investigation so far, have it investigate the same question from scratch.
choices.B: Remove Grep from allowed_tools and have it continue the investigation by reading files with Read thereafter.
choices.C: Send /compact as a prompt with the findings to retain attached, and continue in the same session.
choices.D: Raise max_turns and continue the investigation in the same session.

question:
An airline is building a customer support resolution agent that handles reservation changes and baggage inquiries. The agent loop is a custom implementation that calls the Messages API directly; it repeats the process “call Claude, and if it requests a tool, execute it and return the result” up to three times, then returns the response text at that point to the customer.

In one month of logs, among cases requiring four or more tool calls (get_customer, lookup_order, seat availability search, reservation change), such as arranging a rebooking onto another flight, 18% ended with the response “ただいま確認しています”. Meanwhile, simple inquiries complete in the first iteration.

Which are appropriate ways to revise the loop termination logic? (Select two.)

choices.A: Determine to end the loop if the response text contains a phrase such as “completed.”
choices.B: Raise the iteration limit from 3 to 10 and return the 10th response to the customer as the final answer.
choices.C: Keep the iteration limit large as a safeguard, and log it as an anomaly if it is reached.
choices.D: Continue if stop_reason is "tool_use", and end the loop on "end_turn".
